title: Problem generating homes on the first pass with GPT astra + unity/blender
author: Virtue_Driven
selftext:
I need to make multiple homes. Whenever i try it always deviates from blueprints and has objects protruding into other rooms, requiring manual inspections and lots of edits.

Is there anything I can do to get accurate buildings on the first pass? Prompt tricks?

comments.author: Creepy-Doughnut-5054
comments.body: Try claude. But honestly, if your blueprints are really good, with all the information like dimensions, proportions, margins. scale and so on, Astra absolutely should do the great job. So probably your instructions/blueprints are bad.

replies.author: Virtue_Driven
replies.body: I'll look through them again and see if there were any issues with the blueprints.

replies.author: FuzzyBench3638
replies.body:
Like this guy said inspect your codex project first. Then I would create a imagegen of each house with multiple angles to help blender and then refine that. Do one house at a time. After your first house ask it to do a pass at each house using the method that worked for the first house. For quality results you need to orchestrate. At some point you could ask for it to make a /house skill. 

Just remember the one shot game idea you see on Reddit is a pipe dream for now putting out garbage and eating tokens. Build your systems but don’t spend too much time on “tools” just processes. If this process turns into a skill that works you can then ask it to make a agent that can be deployed to make houses within a prompt

comments.author: cheyumaama
comments.body: There's no such thing as one prompt does it all. You will need to iterate and fix everything. Claude can playtest and fix it a little bit, but at the end, you will have to ask for specific edits yourself

comments.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
comments.body: I have been getting perfect dimentions on my houses with Astra/Claude+Blender, but usually have to iterate on the details. Maybe you are doing too much in one promot? Is it possible to divide the task?

replies.author: Virtue_Driven
replies.body:
I've considered doing it room by room, im just worried that joining it together will create more pains than it prevents.

I think I'm going to have it be a bit more in depth with the blueprints and make sure i'm not missing anything

comments.author: AN1mbleNavigator
comments.body: Your problem is trying to one shot it, either iterate, break a pipeline down into multiple steps it doesn’t do in one run. Or try using sub agents to break the task up.

replies.author: Virtue_Driven
replies.body:
That's been my solution and this is the golden rule. I'd like to reduce how many gens I need to do in order to avoid flaws that I feel ai should be able to avoid.

Example: Despite my requests, on first pass it refuses to double check corners to make sure they meet naturally, and arn't just two walls lined up in a way that leaves an empty square divet at every corner.

I am considering it may be a limit on usage per gen. That being said trying astra medium/hard did not make a difference.

Either way I think that for the time being your comment is the current meta
